main_text.p: qui e non excedunt ipsorum jurisdictionem, si-ve à Paribus aut inferioribus, sicalternando aut ob-secrando? Exempla sunt obvia: Asa2. Chron. 15. & IosaphatIbid. 34., EsraEsra 10. & NehemiasNehem. 10., adjurant omnes subditos vt fideliter Deo inseruiant. Paulus obtestatus est RomanosRom. 12., per miserationes Dei, & obtestatur Timotheum1 Tim. 6. etiam atque etiam in conspectu Dei & Domini Iesu Christi2 Tim. 4., vt quod suum[?] esset[?] munus fideliter obirent. Sed in re non expectata, & non necessaria, hoc fecit Saul; & tamen hîc quàm promptam obseruamus multitudinis obedientiam, & quàm submissam erga Superiorem reuerentiam.

Attendite autem quid Ego inde colligo, (Bene) (Durè)? Tanti [?] ferementiae cum controversia & difficili Alterius[?] lucrimentum[?], et nostri proprij in rebus licitis, et commodo vestro interuentibus[?] a hobis[?] susceptis, non religiosior habenda esset ratio, vt caetera, quae hic sunt obvia, sepona[?], et colligam illud, quod nos Academicos praecipuè afficiat: Duraverunt[?] nos obstringimur[?] (ergo) nos[?] ad obediendum[?] [illegible, ~6 letters]

page.notes: The scan is cut off at the bottom edge, so the last line is incomplete. Several words in the body are doubtful because of ink bleed and show-through from the reverse side; they are marked [?]. The top-right citation "Act. 2.2.4.9.9a" is unreadable; I have omitted it rather than guess. The mark "§ 1.3.8.3" in the lower right margin is also doubtful and is not placed in the text. The page number "§ 2" at top right may be a signature rather than a page number. No catchword is visible.
